dependency_surface_label: Example State official voter-information third-party dependency and external-origin fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Third-party dependency controls keep the first-party answer lane legible when external scripts, embeds, or other vendor-managed resources slow down, break, or are blocked, but they do not replace content correctness, identity assurance, or ordinary help routing.
first_party_core_answer_note: Critical public-answer routes expose the core answer, next-step guidance, and official help/contact lane from first-party controlled content rather than waiting on an external-origin reveal.
non_primary_embed_boundary_note: Heavy embeds and vendor widgets are treated as supplemental or offscreen content unless the office publishes a first-party equivalent or fallback right on the route.
external_origin_failure_fallback_note: If a third-party origin is blocked, filtered, slow, or unavailable, the route still exposes a visible first-party answer or help lane instead of degrading into a partial shell.
tag_manager_and_experiment_scope_note: Critical public-answer routes keep tag-manager and experiment scope intentionally narrow and periodically reviewed so external additions do not quietly outrank the answer lane.
allowed_origin_or_csp_review_note: The office reviews CSP, sandbox, and allowed-origin posture against the dependency inventory so security hardening or vendor changes do not silently erase the route.
